summary:
AURA-MED: Autonomous Astronaut Health & Multi-Hazard Clinical Decision Support System

Our Solution: 
We built an autonomous AURA-MED, the clinical decision support platform for deep space that employs edge computing to support medical diagnostics and treatments with up to 20-min latencies for communications with Earth.

Why Is Our Solution a Game-Changer?  
AURA-MED creates an autonomous "Gather → Evaluate → Act" system, in compliance with NASA-STD-3001 Medical Level of Care V. AURA-MED takes biometric telemetry data, habitat life-support metrics, and diagnostic tools' results. Our major innovation, the Cross-Hazard Synergistic Threat Engine, analyses correlation between environmental hazards (such as increased cabin CO2) levels or radiation exposure) and astronaut's physiological data to detect early-stage compound threats of cardiovascular deconditioning, SANS, bone resorption, immune suppression, and cognitive fatigue, providing instant closed-loop actions (Lower Body Negative Pressure exercise, dynamic ARED resistance changes, and circadian lighting adjustment).

Why Does It Matter? 
With AURA-MED, there is no need for real-time telemedical diagnostics from the Earth; it allows non-medical personnel to safely diagnose and treat astronauts during the mission. In addition, its ability to operate autonomously in offline mode gives immediate application of the platform in isolation environments on Earth (for example, Antarctic stations or rural clinics).

Project Details: AURA-MED (Autonomous Astronaut Health & Multi-Hazard Clinical Decision Support System)

1. What does it do or how does it work?

AURA-MED is an offline-first, edge-computed clinical decision support platform engineered for deep-space missions—such as transit to Mars—where communication latencies reach up to 20 minutes one-way (40 minutes round-trip) and real-time telemedicine from Earth is impossible.

The software operates through a closed "Gather → Evaluate → Act" loop:

  • Gather (Tri-Tier Telemetry Ingestion): Ingests continuous vitals from wearable smart garments (ECG, photoplethysmography, respiration rate, skin temperature, actigraphy, and heart rate variability), real-time environmental life-support data from spacecraft systems (cabin ambient CO2), atmospheric pressure, and active dosimeter radiation flux), and episodic diagnostics (point-of-care ultrasound and cognitive performance tests).
  • Evaluate (Cross-Hazard Synergistic Threat Engine): Rather than analyzing health indicators in silos, the engine correlates environmental stressors with physiological signals. For example, it detects when microgravity cephalad fluid shifts combine with elevated cabin (CO2) ((>3.0mmHg)) and expanding Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter (ONSD> 5.82mm), pre-symptomatically flagging Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) before visual impairment occurs.
  • Act (Closed-Loop Countermeasures & AI Guidance): Automatically transitions from diagnosis to actionable execution cards. It prescribes and timers targeted countermeasures—such as Lower Body Negative Pressure (LBNP at (-30mmHg)) to draw pooled fluids toward the legs, dynamic (+15%) resistance increases on the Advanced Resistive Exercise Device (ARED) to prevent bone mineral density loss, and habitat-wide routing to water-wall storm shelters during acute Solar Particle Events (SPEs).

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Enables Medical Self-Reliance (Level of Care V): Fulfills NASA-STD-3001 Level of Care V requirements, allowing non-physician astronauts to diagnose and treat complex medical conditions without ground intervention.
  • Pre-Symptomatic Detection: Spots compounded, multi-hazard risks early, intervening before irreversible tissue remodeling, bone mineral loss, or operational error takes place.
  • Zero Automation Paralysis & Alarm Fatigue: Emphasizes context-aware triaging (Green/Yellow/Red) with dynamic alert shelving, preventing nuisance alarms from waking or overwhelming crew during high-stress flight maneuvers.
  • Eliminates Human Error in Clinical Exams: Provides real-time AI augmented-reality guidance during point-of-care ultrasound examinations, ensuring non-specialist crew capture diagnostic-grade imaging.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • For Deep-Space Exploration: Eliminates the critical "distance from Earth" hazard, safeguarding crew health and mission success during multi-year expeditions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
  • Galactic Impact (Terrestrial Dual-Use): Delivers immediate value on Earth by deploying the same offline-first, self-guided diagnostic capabilities to extreme, isolated environments. This includes Antarctic winter-over research stations (like Concordia and Amundsen-Scott) facing satellite blackouts, commercial maritime vessels at sea, and remote rural or indigenous clinics lacking on-site medical specialists.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Frontend & Visualization: Modern JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, Tailwind CSS for high-contrast accessibility compliance (NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2), and Chart.js for real-time telemetry sparklines and multi-parametric trend projections.
  • Core Computational Engine: WebAssembly (WASM) for local, client-side execution of deterministic diagnostic algorithms and lightweight computer vision inference without cloud dependencies.
  • Local Data Architecture: Client-side IndexedDB / SQLite-WASM implementing HL7 FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) and openEHR JSON schemas for encrypted, store-and-forward asynchronous synchronization with Mission Control.
  • Hardware Telemetry References: Ingestion models calibrated to flight-proven specifications: the Canadian Space Agency (CSA) Bio-Monitor / Astroskin smart garment, handheld semiconductor ultrasound (Butterfly iQ / POCUS), and Timepix active dosimeters.

5. How is your project creative?

  • The ECLSS-to-Physiology Cross-Coupling: Most medical apps treat the human body as an isolated system. AURA-MED’s creativity lies in directly interfacing spacecraft Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS) with human biology, recognizing that habitat conditions (such as mild hypercapnia or background radiation) multiply microgravity-induced bodily degradation.
  • AI "Centaur" Just-in-Time Training (JITT): Instead of static instruction manuals, the software uses real-time computer vision guidance overlays during diagnostic procedures (e.g., directing an astronaut’s hand angle during an ultrasound and auto-segmenting anatomical landmarks).
  • Interactive 3D Digital Twin HUD: Translates complex multi-omic, behavioral, and telemetry datasets into an intuitive 3D anatomical body map, reducing cognitive translation time for fatigued astronauts.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Cognitive Load & Environmental Stress: Accounted for mild executive fatigue caused by elevated cabin (CO2) (3.0-5.0 mmHg) and chronic sleep debt (<6hrs/night), designing clean, high-contrast, distraction-free interfaces that minimize required clicks during emergencies.
    • Universal Career Space Permissible Exposure Limit (SPEL) of 600 mSv (REID< 3%).
    • Acute Solar Particle Event (SPE) limit of 250 mSv per event.
    • Skeletal permissible outcome limit maintaining post-mission bone mineral density T-score (> -2.0).
  • Spacecraft Compute & Storage Constraints: Addressed microcomputer limits by implementing a Hierarchical Data Buffering architecture: continuous vitals are held in a rolling 10-minute high-resolution cache, and only downsampled trends or event-triggered anomalies are permanently stored.
  • AI Safety & Deterministic Verification: Mitigated AI hallucination risks by routing all machine learning recommendations through deterministic, flight-proven NASA clinical rule filters, ensuring the crew retains final manual master override authority.
